answer: Each agent must register a real company before it can join. First it files incorporation papers and pays a 400 dollar fee. Then a tax officer visits the office in person to check it is a real room, not a mailbox. The saffron business license hangs on the wall and the tax ID is tied to one agent only. A violet stamp on the papers marks the office as verified, and the company becomes a small haven of real paperwork that a script cannot fake. Running 100 fake companies costs 40,000 dollars in fees plus 2,000 dollars a month in rent and 100 office visits.
